title: Gates, phase & interference
source: Lecture Slides - 1 to 7.pdf, PDF pages 21–28 and 49–54; Practice Problems Q6–9.
objectives: Convert relative phase into measurement statistics.
body:
Operations preserve normalization

A closed-system quantum gate is unitary: U†U = I. The Hadamard gate maps |0⟩ to |+⟩ and |1⟩ to |−⟩. The Z gate leaves |0⟩ unchanged and negates the amplitude of |1⟩.

Work through H → Z → H

Start in |0⟩. The first H prepares (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2. Z changes this to (|0⟩−|1⟩)/√2. The final H gives |1⟩. The phase difference becomes a deterministic measurement outcome. Matrix multiplication writes the same sequence as HZH|0⟩, with the rightmost operator acting first.

Same probabilities, different states

|+⟩ and |−⟩ have identical computational-basis measurement probabilities. Applying H before measurement distinguishes them.

Use the existing gate lab

Try Pauli Z on |+⟩, then compare with Z on |0⟩. Predict the end point before playing each rotation. The supplied animation is retained as a separate lab.

Open Pauli gate / Bloch sphere lab ↗

quiz.question: What is the result of H → Z → H applied to |0⟩?
quiz.explanation: H prepares |+⟩, Z turns it into |−⟩, and H maps |−⟩ to |1⟩.

exercise: Solve Q6–9. Compare XZ|ψ⟩ and ZX|ψ⟩: do their different signs imply distinguishable physical states?
solution: XZ = −ZX. For any input the outputs differ by global phase −1, so they give identical statistics for all measurements.
